lesson.title: Prefix Flight Path
lesson.subtitle: Spot the prefix at the sentence end across bracket sentences — and rebuild with modals

hook.title: Watching Things Fly
hook.content: Every separable verb in a real sentence sends its prefix on a flight: the root lands in position 2, the prefix touches down at the very end. Ich mache das Fenster auf. Ich nehme das Essen mit. Ich wache früh auf. Your job: spot the landing. Then the advanced drill — rebuild each sentence inside a modal bracket, where the prefix is grounded again: Ich will das Fenster aufmachen (the whole verb, prefix included, closes the bracket). Flight and grounding, same verb, two architectures.

footnotes.title: The Landing Strip Is Also the Perfekt Spot
footnotes.content: The prefix lands exactly where participles and bare infinitives land — the sentence's final slot is German's cargo bay. When a separable verb goes Perfekt, the prefix flies BACK to the front of the participle: aufgemacht. One slot, three cargoes, one system.

pattern.title: Flight Plans
pattern.content: Flight mode (root in 2, prefix last): Ich rufe ihn an (I call him up — anrufen, the phone verb!). Ich wache früh auf. Wir kaufen? no — Wir sehen die? — keep: Ich schlafe? — Ich schlafe nicht ein? — Ich schlafe ein (I fall asleep). Grounded mode (modal bracket): Ich will ihn anrufen. Du musst früh aufwachen. Wir können nicht einschlafen. Perfekt mode (prefix + ge): Ich habe ihn angerufen. Er ist eingeschlafen. Three modes, one verb — read the mode from the sentence architecture before you translate a word.
pattern.linguist_note: anrufen (call up) proves the particles are spatial even in abstract uses: the phone call goes UP and OUT. English 'call up' kept the spatial image — the particle, not the verb, carries the metaphor in both languages.

exercises.prompt: Spot the landing: 'Morgen fahre ich früh _____.' (depart — abfahren):
exercises.meaning: Morgen fahre ich früh ab = I'm departing early tomorrow
exercises.explanation: abfahren: the root fahre holds position 2, the prefix ab lands at the end — DE-part. Gleich fahre ich ab works too: the flight path even fronted gleich (right away) without grounding anything.

exercises.prompt: Ground it: 'Ich will früh _____.' (to wake up, joined at the end of the modal bracket):
exercises.meaning: Ich will früh aufwachen = I want to wake up early
exercises.explanation: Inside the modal bracket the verb stays WHOLE — prefix included: will opens, aufwachen closes. Feelings ride the cargo hold as whole nouns too: Angst haben, Hoffnung haben — and deine Meinung (your opinion) keeps its ein-family endings: Ich kenne deine Meinung.

exercises.prompt: Three modes of one verb — match. Then recall earlier vocabulary in the short phrases:
exercises.target_answer: Ich kaufe morgen ein, Ich will morgen einkaufen, Ich habe eingekauft, einkaufen, Wir können zumachen, Wir können anmachen, Wir können abmachen, Wir können mitnehmen, Wir können aussuchen, Das Haus kann gut aussehen, das ist traurig, Wir können morgen aufstehen
exercises.meaning: flight mode; grounded mode (modal); Perfekt mode (prefix + ge); dictionary form; We can close; We can turn on; We can arrange; We can take along; We can choose; The house can look good; that is sad; We can get up tomorrow
exercises.explanation: Flight (prefix last), grounding (whole in the bracket), Perfekt (prefix + ge + stem + t) — read the mode first. einkaufen = ein + kaufen: shop 'in', buy in.

exercises.prompt: What English phrasal verb is the twin of 'anrufen' (the verb is 'call')?
exercises.explanation: Both languages kept the spatial metaphor of the phone call going up — an = on/up, and the call goes out. Und wenn es dunkel ist, rufe ich an: the flight path works after dark too.

können opens, nicht rides inside, einschlafen closes WHOLE — grounded flight, negated cargo. The basement knows feelings too: Ich weiß, dass du Sorge hast — und weil ich traurig bin, gehen wir nicht einkaufen.

summary.outcome: Track separable prefixes across flight, grounded, and Perfekt modes.

use_example.english: I want to wake up early.

summary.takeaway: Prefix lands at the sentence end in flight, stays whole in modal brackets, rides the participle in Perfekt — read the mode, then the verb.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Next: ver ↔ for- — the inseparable cognate set: vergessen = forget, and the payoff of every preview.

twist.prompt: Without looking back — rebuild the core sentence from Prefix Flight Path (We cannot fall asleep):
twist.explanation: Re-assembling "Wir können nicht einschlafen" from scratch locks in the structural pattern of Prefix Flight Path without relying on short-term echo.

mitnehmen.context_translation: I want to take the food away / to go.

anrufen.etymology_derivation: Separable: an + rufen (to call/cry); rufen is kin to Old English hrōpan 'to shout'. [wiktionary]

aufwachen.etymology_derivation: Separable: auf (up) + wachen (to be awake/watch); wachen and wake are one verb — a shepherd 'wacht' the flock. [wiktionary]

können.context_translation: I can come / I am able to come.
können.etymology_derivation: Originally meant "to know/understand". Preserved in English "can", "cunning" (knowing how), "uncanny", and "beyond my ken" (beyond my knowledge).

wollen.etymology_derivation: Retains original Germanic sense of desire/intent: "free will", "will to live", "against my will", and "willingly" (cf. Latin voluntary).

müssen.context_translation: I must / have to go now.
müssen.etymology_derivation: Cognate with English "must" (root shifted to sibilant -ss-).

einkaufen.etymology_derivation: ein (in) + kaufen (to buy) — buy in, do the shopping; the kaufen root is the German twin of English cheap. [wiktionary]

abfahren.etymology_derivation: ab (off) + fahren (to drive): to drive off — the same verb root as English fare. [wiktionary]

sorge.etymology_derivation: From Proto-Germanic *surgo — the page lists English sorrow as the cognate: the same care-root that grew into sorrow. [wiktionary]

gleich.etymology_derivation: From Proto-Germanic *galīkaz, having the same form, built from ga- plus the ancestor of -like; the English twin is alike, and the suffix inside it is the same element as English -like and -ly. [wiktionary]

meinung.context_phrase: Meiner Meinung nach ist der Film gut.
meinung.context_translation: In my opinion the film is good.
meinung.etymology_derivation: meinen (to mean) + -ung; the page compares English meaning — your opinion is what you mean. [wiktionary]

weiß.etymology_derivation: t → ß. Also first-person of wissen (ich weiß = I know/am wise).

traurig.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *dreuzagaz — English dreary is the cognate, with English d ↔ German t. [wiktionary]

angst.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *angustiz; the page names no English cognate (anguish/angry not cited) — treat as memorize. [wiktionary]

hoffnung.etymology_derivation: hoffen (to hope) + -ung: German hardened English p into pf-f, so hope became hoffen; the page lists English hoping as the cognate. [wiktionary]
